summary: Revision fixed most round-1 issues: 'Keep' default with opt-in drops, local-only verifier and report runner, DPIA/notice template, attribution, no Sysmon redistribution. New exposure: the monthly client evidence report and PCI/HIPAA mapping become attestations clients hand to auditors and insurers. Liability terms and E&O remain unwritten. Cross-MSSP benchmark and Wazuh GPL need care.

objections.objection: The product now issues client-facing evidence: a monthly PDF with 'coverage status' and per-pack PCI DSS 10 / HIPAA 164.312(b) mapping. MSSP clients will attach it to audit evidence or cyber-insurance questionnaires. If drift went undetected or the mapping is read as 'compliant', a misstatement to an insurer can jeopardise cover, and the claim chain runs MSSP to QuietWin. The lawyer-reviewed agreement with liability cap, no-completeness warranty and E&O cover is still listed as a need, not done, and the report needs explicit 'not a compliance attestation' wording and a stated verification time window.

The opt-in cross-MSSP coverage benchmark pools data derived from MSSPs' client estates (coverage state, drift, event volumes). MSSPs' client contracts usually make that confidential, so 'opt-in' must mean the end client's consent too, and the data must be aggregated and de-identified with a written data-use policy. Otherwise it contradicts the 'no data leaves the client' promise.
objections.evidence: concept:revision_log (defensibility: opt-in cross-MSSP coverage benchmark); concept:risks[1]

objections.objection: Wazuh's licence states GPLv2 covers its decoders, rules and data files, and treats integrating them as a derivative work. Paid packs that copy or modify stock Wazuh rules or decoders must be distributed under GPLv2, which undermines the 'paid content' tier; new rules should be written from scratch or the paid value kept in services and the report runner.

The PCI DSS mapping must cover retention, not just event selection: PCI DSS v4 Req. 10.5.1 asks for 12 months of audit log history with 3 months immediately available, and Wazuh archives are off by default. 'Archive guidance' needs to state required retention per framework, or the mapping overstates what the pack delivers. HIPAA 164.312(b) is a broad standard and should be described as supporting it, not satisfying it.

The verifier and packs run with admin rights on client hosts via RMM and change audit policy. A faulty or compromised pack is a supply-chain incident across many tenants. Signed packs and staged rings are planned, but the agreement should spell out change-approval responsibility (the MSSP authorises each rollout) so the founder isn't the de facto change owner.

strongest_point: Still ships content and local tooling, not a hosted log service; 'Keep' default and opt-in documented drops align with data minimisation without creating logging-duty breaches.
what_would_change_my_mind: A signed, lawyer-reviewed subscription agreement with liability cap, no-completeness warranty and MSSP-owned change approval
A sample client report with 'not a compliance attestation' wording and a dated coverage-verification window
Tech E&O quote under $2k/year bound before the first paid pilot
A written benchmark data-use policy requiring end-client consent and aggregation thresholds
Per-framework retention guidance (PCI 12/3 months) included in the mapping
Confirmation that paid Wazuh rules and decoders are original work, not modified stock rules

resolved_prior.objection: Volume reduction can push clients below their logging or retention duties; liability if a dropped event is needed
resolved_prior.note: 'Keep' is the default, drops are opt-in and documented, archives are the safety net and PCI/HIPAA mapping was added. The residual contract and E&O gap moves into the new report-attestation objection.

resolved_prior.objection: Logon evidence report is employee monitoring (GDPR, DPIA, BetrVG s.87 works councils)
resolved_prior.note: A monitoring notice and DPIA template ship with the report, and the risk is stated. The controller duty stays with the client, which is correct.

resolved_prior.objection: Data custody in the tuning engagement and log-diet script
resolved_prior.note: Verifier and report runner run locally inside the MSSP environment; hosting logs is out of scope; DPA and NDA for onboarding. The benchmark is a new, smaller custody question.

resolved_prior.objection: Upstream licence duties (Sigma DRL, CC BY, MIT)
resolved_prior.note: sysmon-modular is credited and Sigma authors are credited in packs and outputs. Wazuh GPL is a new, separate licence point.

resolved_prior.objection: Sysinternals licence forbids redistributing standalone Sysmon
resolved_prior.note: RMM scripts fetch Sysmon from Microsoft; stated in risks.

resolved_prior.objection: Public drop list tells attackers what clients are blind to
resolved_prior.note: The public baseline is the 'Keep' profile; 'Lean' drop rationale is in the paid tier.
